clue.text: National anthem's intro upset Crimean

definitions.note: a noun here: a citizen of a country

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so only the first letter of the word is kept
something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of anthem
the letters of Crimean rearranged

explanation.surface: A country's national anthem begins with something that annoys a person from Crimea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' looks like an adjective attached to 'anthem', but it stands alone as a noun meaning a citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the United States is a national of that country, so an American is one example.

clue.text: Structure not present around entrance to Renaissance church

indicators.note: an entrance is the way in, so only the first letter of the following word is used
around says the first piece is wrapped about the others

blocks.note: someone not present is away
the first letter of Renaissance
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A Renaissance church whose doorway stands empty, with nobody about.
explanation.definitionFit: An archway is a built opening under an arch, a kind of architectural structure.

clue.text: Young swimmer at all times grabbing line

indicators.note: something grabbing holds another thing within its grip

blocks.note: ever means always
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A young swimmer who is forever clutching the lane rope or a fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish that swims, so a young swimmer is a fair description.

clue.text: Example tutorials in start of live broadcast

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of live

explanation.surface: Teaching sessions shown at the beginning of a live television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing tutorials inside something, but its two letters are part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An illustration can be an instance used to explain a point, so it is a synonym of example.

clue.text: Sadly does not finish on minute mission

indicators.note: a word that does not finish has its final letter cut off

blocks.note: alas is the cry of sorrow, equivalent to sadly
a mo is a moment, a minute

explanation.surface: Regrettably someone fails to complete a mission against the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo was a Spanish mission in Texas, famous for its 1836 siege.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo in San Antonio was built as a Catholic mission station, so it is a proper-noun example of one.

clue.text: Heroin drop outside clubs

indicators.note: outside says one piece sits around the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: to sag is to droop or drop
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Drugs being dropped outside nightclubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scag is a slang name for heroin, the drug, used mostly in British and American street speech.

clue.text: Blue brief thought that's poisonous

definitions.note: describes the answer, a poisonous substance, rather than naming it

indicators.note: making a word brief clips its last letter off

blocks.note: cyan is a greenish blue colour
an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: A gloomy passing thought that turns out to be toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyanide is a notoriously deadly compound, the stuff that is poisonous in countless murder mysteries.

clue.text: US soldier allowed jacket

blocks.note: GI is the standard term for an American soldier
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An American soldier given permission to wear a particular jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A gilet is a sleeveless padded jacket or waistcoat, a garment of the jacket family.

clue.text: Boxer wielded bats when overwhelmed by force

indicators.note: bats is slang for crazy, so the letters go mad and are scrambled
something overwhelmed is engulfed, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: might is strength or force
the letters of wielded rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer swinging baseball bats until overpowered by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the thing wielded, but it is the anagram signal meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A middleweight is a boxer of a particular weight class, between welterweight and light heavyweight.

clue.text: Courteous assembly of Roman cardinals

blocks.note: C, IV, I and L are Roman numerals, ie cardinal numbers written the Roman way, put together

explanation.surface: A polite gathering of Catholic cardinals in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinals look like churchmen but are cardinal numbers; C is 100, IV is 4, I is 1, L is 50.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil means polite and well-mannered, a straightforward synonym of courteous.

clue.text: David's wife advanced with considerable trouble

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for advanced
big means considerable
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: King David's wife moved forward despite great difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Abigail married King David after the death of her first husband Nabal.

clue.text: Mostly cautious conflict

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: wary means cautious

explanation.surface: A conflict fought largely with caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A war is an armed conflict between nations or groups, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Swirling wind and frost — something not unrelated?

definitions.note: a cryptic hint: the answer is connected to the wind and frost just mentioned

indicators.note: swirling means whirling round, so the letters spin into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of wind and frost, without the link

explanation.surface: A wintry scene of whirling gusts and hard frost, with something else connected to them.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is deliberately vague: a snowdrift is piled up by wind in freezing weather, so it is certainly related to the fodder words. 'and' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdrifts are heaps of snow formed by wind in cold conditions, so they are closely tied to wind and frost.

clue.text: Something eaten by 20 in tent

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a yurt is a round Mongolian tent
20 across is OWN GOAL, abbreviated to OG on football scoresheets

explanation.surface: Food consumed by number 20 while sitting in a tent.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 20 refers to the answer to 20 across, whose abbreviation OG appears in match reports.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt is a food, so it is something that gets eaten, a loose descriptive definition.

clue.text: French department's income-benefit cheque in good shape at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: a giro was the British state benefit payment cheque
the last letters of in, good and shape

explanation.surface: A welfare cheque from a French administrative department arrives in decent condition at last.
explanation.walkthrough: A giro was the cheque by which British unemployment benefit was once paid. 'in good shape' looks like a phrase meaning healthy, but each word only lends its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gironde is one of the administrative departments of France, around Bordeaux.

clue.text: Facing bearing of 45 degrees when entering turn

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to veer is to turn
northeast is the compass bearing at 45 degrees

explanation.surface: Navigation instructions: face a 45-degree heading as you take the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin decorative facing glued over a cheaper surface, so it is a synonym in the noun sense.

clue.text: Again introduce remorseful sort that's relinquished power

indicators.note: having relinquished something means giving it up, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: a repenter is someone who feels remorse
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A contrite former official giving up power and making a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-enter can mean to enter or input again, as with data, which is to introduce it a second time.

clue.text: Platform for opponents engaging with Napoleon?

definitions.text: Platform for opponents engaging with Napoleon?

blocks.clueFragment: Platform for opponents engaging with Napoleon
blocks.note: surface reading: a stage or battlefield for enemies fighting the French emperor
setter's reading: Napoleon is also a trick-taking card game, so the platform is a piece of furniture where players sit against each other

explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon (or Nap) is an old card game; the question mark flags that the emperor is not meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a card game face their opponents across a table made for cards, the surface that hosts the contest.

clue.text: Singers from India crushed by endless routine task

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter goes
crushed by suggests being squeezed in the middle of the other piece

blocks.note: a chore is a routine task
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A troupe of singers from India worn down by monotonous daily work.
explanation.walkthrough: CHORE loses its last letter to become CHOR, and I goes between O and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of singers, typically performing together in church or concert.

clue.text: Dish from eg Estonia unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means the word stops short, missing its last letter

blocks.note: Estonia is one of the Baltic states

explanation.surface: An Estonian dish left half-cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry dish cooked and served in a metal bowl, popular in Birmingham, England.

clue.text: Setter abandoning recurrent idea for article

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so those letters are left out

blocks.note: a theme is a recurring idea in a work
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A crossword setter dropping a pet theme when writing a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: The is the definite article in grammar, so it is a word-class example of an article.

clue.text: Sentimental, tense, brief message

blocks.note: twee means sentimental or overly quaint
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A short post that is both mawkish and anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Twee is a British word for affectedly cute or sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweet is a short post on the social network X, formerly Twitter, so a brief message.

clue.text: Net deposit possibly contributing to loss?

definitions.text: Net deposit possibly contributing to loss?

blocks.clueFragment: Net deposit possibly contributing to loss
blocks.note: surface reading: a sum paid into a bank after deductions that still ends in a financial loss
setter's reading: something deposited in the goal net, by a player from the wrong team, helping their own side lose

explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' looks like the accounting word for after-deductions; it is a football goal net.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the ball into one's own team's net scores for the opposition, which can contribute to losing the match.

clue.text: Rather large selection from meagre attempts

indicators.note: a selection from a phrase is a run of its letters picked out intact

blocks.note: the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A fair number taken from a set of feeble efforts.
explanation.definitionFit: Great means large in size or amount, so it serves as a synonym for rather large.

clue.text: Jupiter and Earth finally linked to each satellite in solar system

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the two named words

blocks.note: the last letter of Jupiter
the last letter of Earth
EA is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: An astronomy note on how Jupiter and Earth relate to every moon in the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhea is the second-largest moon of Saturn, a natural satellite within our solar system.

clue.text: Despot ultimately deployed contrived riot act?

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the next word is used
something contrived is artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of deployed
the letters of riot act rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant reading out a staged riot act to troops.
explanation.walkthrough: To read the riot act is to issue a stern warning; the question mark hints at a despot doing exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictator is a ruler with absolute power, a direct synonym of despot.
